title: Output probability during rewind
statement: Let $N$ be a finite nondeterministic Turing machine over Boolean inputs, let $x$ be an input, and let $r,T$ be natural numbers. Suppose every length-$T$ choice word makes $N$ halt on $x$ from its initial configuration. For any Boolean value $v$, any $i\in\mathbb N$, and any $j$ with $0\le j\le r$ and $j+i=r$, take a counter $c$ with $0\le c\le r+1$ and an augmented configuration $C$ in rewind phase at $(j,c)$ with empty output and all later blocks blank with their heads at $0$. If $c\le j+1$, then the probability that a uniformly chosen Boolean word of length $i(T+|x|+2)+1$ makes the amplified machine from $C$ output exactly the one-symbol word $[v]$ equals the probability that, for a uniformly chosen Boolean word of length $iT$, the decision function applied to $c$ plus the number of its $i$ consecutive length-$T$ blocks on which $N$ outputs exactly $[\mathrm{true}]$ equals $v$.
